Quick startThe everyday tasks, one card each
Power

Power On

  1. Go to the Home page on the touch panel. If the keypad appears, enter the touch panel password, 1234, and tap Enter.
  2. Turn on System Power, LED Wall and Amphitheater Lighting, or just the ones you need.
  3. Give the equipment a moment to power up in order before you start.
Audio

Play background music

  1. On the Video page, send your music source to Program or Preview.
  2. Choose whether the PA plays Program audio or Preview audio. Use the touch panel, or the Audio Output Select button on the front of the AVPro Edge switcher in the rack.
  3. Start the music.
Audio

Use a wireless microphone

  1. Take Mic 1 or Mic 2 from the mic drawer. They're labeled.
  2. Turn it on and check the battery.
  3. Open the Audio page in Simple mode and turn that mic up.
Video

Put something on the LED wall

  1. Open the Video page on the touch panel.
  2. Choose the source you want to use.
  3. Check the rack monitor to confirm what's being sent out.
Lighting

Turn on the lights

  1. Open the Lighting page on the touch panel.
  2. Choose a zone on the left, then one of the eight presets.
  3. For finer control, use the CueServer pages on the iPad. See the Lighting section.
Visiting show

Hand off to a visiting console

  1. On the Audio page, select External Console under Audio Mode.
  2. Their mixer plugs into Left and Right In at the stage plate or the AV1 plate.
  3. See Visiting shows for monitors, lighting and video.
Power

Power Off

  1. Bring all levels down and return mics to the drawer.
  2. Set Audio Mode back to Simple if it was changed.
  3. Turn the system off from the Home page.

How the system fits togetherWhere things are and how you control them

Where things are

All of the audio, video and lighting equipment lives in one rack in the AV/IT room of the support building, to the right of the stage. The touch panel is in that same room. Two iPads give you the same controls anywhere on site.

Out in the park you'll find the performance platform and LED wall, lighting columns around the back of the circle, and festoon string lights over the street. The AV1 panel sits in the garden bed across from the stage. It is the front of house connection point for visiting productions.

Ways to control it

Touch panel
The simple way. Power, sources, volume, external console mode and lighting presets. Many buttons change several things at once.
QSYS on the iPad
The same touch panel pages, on an iPad you can carry around.
SQ MixPad on the iPad
Full control of the Allen & Heath mixer for live shows: channel names, levels, EQ and routing. Turn it on by selecting iPad under Audio Mode on the QSYS touch panel.
CueServer app on the iPad
Advanced lighting control: presets, colors and positions for each lighting zone. You may also hear it called the Q Server.

The touch panelQSYS control pages, page by page

Keypad

If the panel shows the keypad, enter the touch panel password, 1234, and tap Enter. Tap Clear to start over if you mistype. All passwords are also listed under Passwords and accounts.

Home

Home is the starting point. Three switches power the system on and off:

System Power
Turns the audio and video system on or off. It powers up and down in the right order on its own.
LED Wall
Turns the LED wall on or off.
Amphitheater Lighting
Turns the show lighting on or off.

Turn on everything at once, or just the parts you need. The bar along the bottom moves between Home, Audio, Video and Lighting.

Audio

Pick an Audio Mode on the left side of the page. The Video Audio fader on the right sets the level of whatever video source is playing, such as Digital Signage. It stays on screen in every mode.

Simple
Everyday use. Faders for Wireless Mic 1 and Wireless Mic 2. Tap the arrows to raise or lower a mic, and tap the mic icon to mute or unmute it.
iPad
Hands mixing to the SQ MixPad app on the iPad for a full live show. The panel shows "Control audio via the SQ MixPad app."
External Console
For a visiting mixer. The panel lists where to plug in, and keeps Wireless Mic 1 and 2 available as announcement microphones.

Video

Choose a source for Preview on the left and for Program on the right. Program is what the LED wall shows. The sources are Digital Signage (the BrightSign player), Bluray, AppleTV and User Device. The LED Wall switch in the middle turns the wall on or off. Check the rack monitor to confirm what's going out.

Lighting

Choose a zone on the left: Stage Wash, Moving Spots, Side Lights, Columns or String Lights. Then tap one of the eight presets. For anything beyond the presets, use the CueServer app.

Amphitheater Lighting
On the Stage Wash, Moving Spots and Side Lights pages. Turns the show lighting on or off.
External Control
On the same three pages. Turn it on to let a visiting lighting controller run the show lights.
Architectural Lighting
On the Columns and String Lights pages. When it's on, these lights turn on automatically at sunset and off at sunrise, in the color scheme you've selected.

AudioPA, wireless mics and the SQ mixer

The main PA

The PA is an L'Acoustics system: five Kiva II cabinets per side, two KS21i subs per side, left and right side fills, and a center fill. Six stage monitor outputs run from the same amplifiers.

Stereo only. The system is tuned as a left and right stereo PA with no separate sub send. Visiting engineers sometimes ask for an aux fed sub. L'Acoustics recommends against it for this system, so the input we offer is stereo Left and Right only.

Background music

Background music plays through the video system, from either Program audio or Preview audio. Choose which one the PA hears on the touch panel, or with the Audio Output Select button on the front of the AVPro Edge switcher in the rack. The lights beside it show OUT1 or OUT2.

This lets the BrightSign keep showing signage on the LED wall from Program while the Apple TV plays music from YouTube or Spotify on Preview.

Wireless mics

Mic 1 and Mic 2 are labeled for everyday use and work from Simple mode on the touch panel Audio page. The antennas are mounted above the stage. Keep the mics in the drawer in the rack.

  1. Turn the mic on and check the battery level on its display.
  2. Turn it up on the touch panel Audio page in Simple mode.
  3. Turn the mic off and return it to the drawer after the event.

The SQ mixer and SQ MixPad

The Allen & Heath SQ rack mixer handles live shows. It has no physical control surface. You run it from the SQ MixPad app on either iPad, with full control of channel names, levels, EQ and routing.

  1. Select iPad under Audio Mode on the QSYS touch panel.
  2. Open SQ MixPad on the iPad and connect to the mixer.
  3. Name your channels and set levels and EQ.
  4. Route inputs from the two stage racks. Together they give you up to 32 stage inputs.

Larger shows that need more inputs should bring their own console and use External Console mode.

More training: when you're in iPad mode and mixing from SQ MixPad, Allen & Heath has further training and guides for the SQ mixer. See the Allen & Heath SQ support center and the SQ resources page.

Video and BrightSignLED wall, switcher, signage

Program and Preview

The video switcher has two outputs. Program feeds the LED wall. Preview is a second picture you can watch on the rack monitor without the audience seeing it. On the rack monitor, the left side is Program and the right side is Preview. The touch panel Video page shows them the other way around, with Preview on the left and Program on the right.

The switcher also chooses whether the PA plays Program audio or Preview audio. See Background music.

Sources

BrightSign player
Signage, graphics and looping content for the LED wall.
Apple TV
Streaming video and music, and AirPlay from a phone or Mac.
Blu ray player
Movie nights. Its audio also feeds the SQ mixer directly for finer control.
Stage video in
A visiting HDMI source through the converter at the stage. See Visiting shows.

LED wall

The LED wall is 19.7 by 11.5 feet at 2112 by 1232 pixels. Its brightness changes automatically with the time of day. To adjust the brightness levels, call Sweetwater Integration support.

Updating BrightSign content

BrightSign content is built and published with BrightSign Author (formerly BrightAuthor:connected). It is a free app for Mac or PC, and it also runs on the web at app.bsn.cloud.

  1. Open BrightSign Author on a computer on the AV network.
  2. Open the Heritage Park presentation, or create one, and add your images or video.
  3. Set a schedule if content should change by day or time.
  4. Publish to the player. Without a cloud subscription, publish over the Local Network.

BrightSign's own guides cover each step in detail: BrightSign Author documentation and Scheduling and Publishing Presentations.

LightingFull lighting control guide

Overview

The CueServer (also called the Q Server) is the brain of the lighting system. The QSYS touch panel gives you basic control through eight presets. The CueServer pages on the iPad give you full control of every fixture: five fixture groups, each with its own page, plus an ALL page for master shutdowns and plaza wide looks.

Stage Wash
8 front wash and 8 rear wash fixtures over the stage.
Moving Spots
4 moving head spot fixtures.
Side Lights
4 side light fixtures.
Columns
14 column lights along Main Street and Burnett Avenue.
String Lights
The overhead string lights across Main Street.
ALL
Master off buttons, Night Mode, the timer and preset mover looks.

Getting around

Every page has a row of navigation buttons along the bottom. Tap a name to jump to that page, or tap Home to return to the start screen. The page you're on is replaced in the navigation bar by its own OFF button in the bottom left corner. For example, the Stage Wash page shows STAGE OFF there.

Home page

The Home page is the start screen: the City of Denison logo with six buttons underneath that open each control page.

  • Stage Wash for the front and rear stage washes
  • Moving Spots for the four moving heads
  • Side Lights for the four side lights
  • Columns for the column lights
  • String Lights for the overhead strings
  • ALL for master offs, Night Mode, the timer and mover looks

The Home page doesn't change any lights by itself. It's only for choosing where to go.

Controls on every fixture page

Each fixture page uses the same layout: presets on the left, fixtures in the middle, color on the right and navigation along the bottom.

Fixture buttons
Each circle or square stands for one light, laid out roughly where it sits on the plaza. Tap a fixture to select it before changing its color or settings. The shape fills with the light's current color so you can see what's on at a glance.
Color wheel
Top right. Tap or drag anywhere on the wheel to pick a color for the selected fixtures. The center is white or pale, and the edge is the most saturated color.
Color faders
The four vertical faders mix color by hand. Slide up to add more of that color, down to remove it. The first three are always red, green and blue. The fourth changes by fixture type and is described on each page below.
Page OFF button
Bottom left. Turns off every fixture on the current page. Other pages aren't affected.

Presets

Presets store a complete look for a page so you can bring it back later. There are eight per page.

  1. Set the lights the way you want them.
  2. Tap a red Save button (1 to 8) to store the look in that slot.
  3. To bring a look back, tap the matching green Load button.
Careful: Save overwrites anything already saved in that slot.

Presets on one page only affect that page's fixtures. Stage Wash preset 1 and Columns preset 1 are separate looks. Presets are named 1 through 8 and can be renamed in CueServer once your looks are set.

Stage Wash

Stage Wash controls the lights that color the stage: a row of 8 Front Wash fixtures and a row of 8 Rear Wash fixtures. Select any mix of front and rear fixtures, then set the color with the wheel or faders.

Faders
Red, green, blue, and a fourth light green fader that adds lime and white to soften or brighten the color.
Zoom
The bottom slider. Slide left for a tight beam, right for a wide spread.
STAGE OFF
Turns off all 16 wash fixtures.

Moving Spots

Moving Spots controls the 4 moving head fixtures: where they point, their beam pattern and their color.

GOBO
Picks the pattern projected in the beam, such as open, dots or breakup.
PAN
Turns the head left and right.
TILT
Tips the head up and down.
FOCUS
Sharpens or softens the edge of the beam or gobo.
ZOOM
Makes the beam narrower or wider.
DIMMER
Brightness, from off to full.

These fixtures mix color with cyan, magenta and yellow faders instead of red, green and blue. The fourth tan fader is CTO, which warms the white toward a tungsten look. The color wheel works the same as on the other pages. MOVERS OFF turns off all 4 moving spots.

Tip: if the movers are on but you see nothing, check that DIMMER is up.

Side Lights

Side Lights controls the 4 side fixtures, shown as a two by two grid. Select one or more fixtures, then set the color with the wheel or faders.

Faders
Red, green, blue, and a fourth bright green fader for lime.
Zoom
The bottom slider, from narrow to wide beam.
SIDE LIGHTS OFF
Turns off all 4 side lights.

Columns

Columns controls the 14 column lights, drawn on a map of the plaza so each square sits where its column stands.

  • Along Main Street, north side: 5 columns across the top.
  • Along Main Street, south side: 5 columns between the street and the stage lawn.
  • Along Burnett Avenue: 4 columns down the left side.

Tap the squares for the columns you want, then set the color. The faders are red, green, blue, and a fourth tan fader for amber or warm white. There's no zoom on this page. COLUMNS OFF turns off all 14 columns.

String Lights

String Lights controls the overhead strands that zigzag across Main Street above the stage lawn. Each dot on the screen is one bulb, drawn in the pattern the strands hang in. Tap single bulbs or a run of bulbs, then set the color.

The faders are red, green, blue, and a fourth white fader for clean white or pastel tints. STRING LIGHTS OFF turns off every strand.

ALL page

The ALL page is the master control. It shuts down groups in one tap, runs the automatic modes and recalls the built in mover looks.

Mode buttons (top row)

The dot on each button lights up when that mode is active.

NIGHT MODE
Switches the plaza to its programmed nighttime look.
TIMER ON
Lets the CueServer's schedule run the lights automatically.
TIMER OFF
Stops the schedule so the lights stay as you set them.

Master OFF buttons

LIVE OFF
Any manual changes made from the control pages.
SIDES OFF
All side lights.
COLUMNS OFF
All column lights.
STRINGS OFF
All string lights.
STAGE OFF
All stage wash fixtures.
MOVERS OFF
All moving spots.

Mover looks (right side)

STAGE MOVERS
Points the movers at the stage.
WALL MAP
Points the movers at the wall.
FIELD OF STARS
A starfield effect across the plaza.

Tap MOVERS OFF to clear any of these looks.

Schedules

The string lights turn on and off on a schedule. Tap TIMER ON on the ALL page to let it run. The on and off times are set in the CueServer app. If you need more help, call Sweetwater Integration support.

Quick how tos

Turn everything off at the end of an event
Go to ALL and tap each OFF button, or tap LIVE OFF to drop manual changes and let the timer take over.
Make the whole stage one color
Open Stage Wash, tap all 16 fixtures, then pick the color on the wheel.
Save a look for next time
Set the lights, then tap a red Save number on that page. Write down which number holds which look.

Visiting showsExternal console mode and the wall plates

What External Console mode does

Selecting External Console under Audio Mode on the touch panel switches the PA over to the Left and Right inputs at the wall plates, so a visiting mixer runs the show through our speakers. Visitors still get our L'Acoustics monitors and amplifiers through the monitor inputs.

The panel lists the connections: Main Left to "Left In" and Main Right to "Right In" at AV1 (front of house) or WP01 (stage), and monitors to "Monitor 1 to 6" at WP01. Wireless Mic 1 and 2 stay available on the panel as announcement microphones.

A visiting lighting controller plugs into the external lighting controller input at either plate. Then turn on External Control on the touch panel Lighting page.

Stage wall plate

Left In · Right InStereo feed from the visiting mixer
Mon 1 to Mon 6Monitor sends in. Mon 1 plays on Mon A, Mon 2 on Mon B, and so on.
Mon A to Mon FSpeaker outputs to the stage monitors
DMX 1 · DMX 2External lighting controller input
Net Tie 1 · 2Network lines to the AV1 plate at front of house
Video InSDI. Use the HDMI to SDI converter for HDMI sources. Mac users can AirPlay to the Apple TV instead, with no cable needed.

AV1 plate (front of house)

The AV1 plate in the garden bed mirrors the stage: Left In, Right In, the external lighting controller input and two Net Tie lines back to the stage. Use either plate for the Left and Right feed, not both.

Visiting show checklist

  1. Tell the visiting engineer the PA takes a stereo Left and Right feed only.
  2. Choose stage or AV1 for their mix position.
  3. Patch Left and Right In, and Mon 1 to 6 if they're using our monitors.
  4. On the touch panel Audio page, select External Console under Audio Mode.
  5. For a visiting lighting controller, patch it into the external lighting controller input and turn on External Control on the Lighting page.
  6. After the show, set Audio Mode back to Simple and turn External Control off so the system returns to normal.

TroubleshootingFollow the questions from the top

Audio No sound from the speakers

Is the system powered on?
YesGo to the next question.NoTurn it on from the Home page and wait for startup.
Is Audio Mode set to External Console?
YesThe PA is listening to the wall plates. Switch to Simple unless a visiting mixer is plugged in.NoGo to the next question.
Is the source or main output muted on the Audio page?
YesUnmute it and raise the level.NoGo to the next question.
Is the audio switch following the correct output?
YesGo to the next question.NoSet it to Program or Preview, whichever the music source is on.
Still nothing? Call Sweetwater Integration support.

Audio A wireless mic isn't working

Does the label on the mic match the one you're turning up?
YesGo to the next question.NoFor simple use, use Mic 1 or Mic 2.
Is the mic on with a charged battery?
YesGo to the next question.NoReplace or charge the batteries.
Is it turned up and unmuted in Simple mode?
YesGo to the next question.NoTurn it up on the Audio page.
In SQ MixPad, is the mic channel on and routed correctly?
YesGo to the next step.NoTurn the channel on and check its routing.
Still nothing? Call Sweetwater Integration support.

Video LED wall is blank

Is the LED wall turned on from the Home page?
YesGo to the next question.NoTurn it on and give it a minute to come up.
Does the left side of the rack monitor show a picture?
YesThe signal is leaving the rack. Call Sweetwater Integration support.NoPick a different Program source. Check the source itself is on and playing.
Still blank? Call Sweetwater Integration support. Don't change settings on the LED wall processor.

Lighting Lights won't respond

Do the lights respond to a preset on the touch panel?
YesYou're all set.NoGo to the next question.
Do they respond in the CueServer app?
YesYou're all set.NoPower cycle the system, then try the touch panel and the CueServer app again.
Still not working? Call Sweetwater Integration support.

Lighting Quick lighting fixes

Lights change on their own
The timer is running. Tap Timer Off on the ALL page.
Movers are on but dark
Raise the Dimmer slider on the Moving Spots page.
A color change did nothing
Select the fixtures first, then change the color.
Loaded the wrong preset
Load the correct number. Nothing is lost by loading.
Saved over a preset
The old look can't be recovered. Rebuild it and save again.
Screen is unresponsive
Contact Sweetwater Integration for service.
